title: cuda-kernel-optimization-notes-flashattention-paged-kv-v5
content:
Context and goal:
These are working notes for CUDA kernel-level optimizations we want to adopt in the serving runtime to improve tail latency and per-token cost. Focus areas: integrating FlashAttention-style attention kernels, fusing common post-attention ops, and supporting a paged KV-cache design that reduces memory pressure for very long contexts and multi-session workloads. This doc captures micro-optimizations, trade-offs, and TODOs for prototyping and benchmarking.

High-level goals:
- Reduce median and P95 per-token latency for short and medium requests (<= 2048 tokens)
- Improve throughput for batched workloads while allowing low-latency single-request paths
- Support page-in/page-out of KV cache to operate within constrained GPU memory for multi-tenant Dedicated nodes
- Maintain deterministic fallback to reference kernels for correctness and debugging

FlashAttention integration notes:
- Benefit: lowers memory bandwidth by computing attention with reduced intermediate storage (no explicit O(N^2) softmax matrix storing), enabling longer sequences and better cache behavior.
- Implementation choices: use FlashAttention v2-style algorithm with block-sum numerically stable softmax via running max/exp sums. Target fp16/bf16 paths on Ampere+ devices with Tensor Cores.
- Memory layout: pack QKV in QKV-interleaved layout to improve coalescing. For multi-head, we should consider (B, H, L, D_head) contiguous in L so that attention reads contiguous sequences. Avoid strided gather when possible.
- Kernel variants to implement:
  - flash_attn_fwd_fp16 (single-threaded kernel launch per head block)
  - flash_attn_fwd_bf16
  - flash_attn_fwd_int8-quantized (later; requires per-head scale/zero-point and clamp handling)
- Use cp.async (CUDA 11.8+/SM80) for L2-prefetch when touching long past KV pages to hide global memory latency. Fall back to async copy + shared memory loads when cp.async not available.
- Tiling: tile over sequence length (L) and head dim (D_head) in a 2D partition. Tune tile sizes for occupancy and register pressure (example: L_tile=128, D_tile=64 for D_head=64). Add autotune table keyed by (seq_len, D_head, SM) collected at build-time.
- Numerics: implement running max trick for numerical stability; test against reference softmax for fp16/bf16 across long sequences for correctness.

Fused ops (post-attention):
- Common pattern in generation: attention -> linear out -> residual add -> layernorm (or rmsnorm) -> activation -> projection. Each of these can be fused in different groupings: we should prototype three fused kernels:
  1) attn+proj+residual_add: avoid writing full attention output to global memory; stream output into projection multiplication (GEMM) and add residual in-register/SMem.
  2) layernorm+mlp-1 (first FC in feed-forward) fused: compute norm then immediately apply FC using registers to hold normalized values to reduce global writes.
  3) combined (1)+(2) where feasible: careful about register pressure and kernel launch time.
- Fusing trade-offs: reduces memory traffic and kernel launch overhead, but increases complexity for mixed-precision and makes profiling harder. Provide flags to enable/disable each fusion for runtime selection.
- API: fused kernels should expose capability flags and expected tensor shapes; runtime will select based on model config & device memory/compute profile.

Paged KV cache design (draft):
- Motivation: models with very long contexts and many concurrent sessions exceed device memory. Instead of storing full KV for every session on GPU, keep a hot-working set of KV pages on device; cold pages on host/NVM.
- Page unit: define PAGE_LEN (e.g., 512 tokens) and store KV per page per layer/head compressed layout. Pages are appended as generation progresses.
- Indexing: maintain a lightweight page directory (on CPU or GPU pinned memory) mapping (session_id, layer, head, page_idx) -> GPU resident flag + device pointer or host pointer. Directory must be small and cacheable.
- Page lifecycle:
  - On request for tokens in a page not resident, issue an async page-in (cudaMemcpyAsync or GPUDirect when available) into a pre-allocated device page buffer pool.
  - Eviction: LRU-ish across pages with heuristics: prefer evicting pages from sessions not recently active and layers with lower reuse. Track per-page last-access timestamp updated on kernel execution.
  - Prefetching: for autoregressive generation, prefetch next page for active sessions when throughput budgets allow.
- Page buffer pool: maintain multiple slots per GPU for concurrent page-ins. Use CUDA streams per session group to overlap data movement with compute.
- Kernel support: FlashAttention and attention kernels should accept a sparse KV accessor: given a request range, kernel reads KV either from contiguous device memory (fast path) or from remapped buffer pointers filled by page-in. Avoid making kernels branch on resident-ness frequently; prefer filling device-resident pointers before kernel launch.
- Consistency: operations that mutate KV (e.g., inserting new KV for generated tokens) must write into the current device page buffer; if page full, flush back to host asynchronously and allocate new page.
- Telemetry: emit metrics for page hit/miss, avg page-in latency, DMA bandwidth usage. Expose thresholds for autoscaling: if page-in rate consistently high, recommend scaling to more GPU memory or moving session to Dedicated capacity.

Scheduling and runtime selection logic:
- Need a policy to choose between: baseline kernels, FlashAttention, fused kernels, and quantized variants. Inputs: model dims (D, H), seq_len distribution, batch_size, device type (SM version, memory bandwidth), quality constraints (exact FP32 required?), and current memory pressure (paged KV status).
- Simple rules to start with:
  - If device >= SM80 and D_head <= 128 and seq_len >= 128 -> prefer FlashAttention fp16/bf16 path.
  - If batch_size==1 and latency_slo tight -> prefer lowest-launch-overhead path (fused kernels) even if slightly higher compute.
  - If memory pressure high and page miss-rate > 5% -> throttle prefetch and favor smaller working set kernels.
- Implement a small runtime autotuner that runs short micro-benchmarks at warm-up to pick best kernel variant and populate a cache keyed by model+device.

Microbenchmarks and validation plan:
- Benchmarks to implement: single-request latency (B=1) at seq_len={32,128,512,2048}, batched throughput (B={1,4,8,16}) at same seq lengths, and multi-session mixed-gen scenario to stress paged KV.
- Collect: latency distribution (P50/P90/P95/P99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory bandwidth, page-in/miss rate.
- Correctness: run end-to-end generation tests vs reference aten kernels; compare outputs with tolerance for fp16/bf16. Also validate numerics when using fused reductions + residuals.

Implementation milestones and TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype FlashAttention kernels integrated into serving runtime (PR skeleton exists: GH #324).
- [ ] Add cp.async-based prefetch path and fallback path (Ava to prototype).
- [ ] Implement basic paged KV layer + page-dir and simple LRU eviction (Miguel + Li).
- [ ] Build small autotuner harness to select kernel variants at model load time.
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks for page metrics and kernel selection decisions.
- [ ] Run cluster-wide soak test with 1000 concurrent sessions to validate eviction/prefetch heuristics.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Best page size? 256 vs 512 vs 1024 tradeoffs: smaller pages reduce wasted memory and latency for partial fetch but increase control overhead. Need cost model and microbenchmarks.
- How to support quantized KV (int8) and packed layouts in paged design while keeping kernel complexity manageable?
- Should fused kernels be maintained as separate code paths or expressed via a kernel composer that generates fused code at build-time? (JIT vs static).
- How to surface failure modes to higher-level runtime (e.g., page-in timeouts, device OOM) without blowing up request latency? Graceful fallback policies needed.

Appendix: quick profile notes (NVPROF / Nsight):
- Observed main hotspots: global memory loads for KV read (~45% bandwidth), softmax kernel memory stores (~20%), post-attn GEMM (~25%).
- Peak occupancy low on certain models due to register pressure in fused kernels; reduce tile sizes or split fused kernels as needed.
- cp.async cut apparent page-in latency by ~30% on SM8x devices in synthetic tests.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a living doc: iterations expected as we collect microbenchmarks. Please add comments inline in Confluence page linked above or comment on GH #324.
- If you plan to work on any TODO, add your name in collaborators and update status when moved to in_review.
